subject: Metering definition and rounding for committed per-token tiers (DataWave)
messages:
From: Amy Liu <amy@datawave.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Metering questions for hosted commit tiers

Rishi,

Thanks again for the briefing yesterday. We pulled sample usage from April and May (attached) and have a few open items before we finalize the monthly commit level: 

1) Streaming sessions: our product keeps long-lived streaming connections where user audio/text flows continuously. Do you measure "streaming tokens" as tokens emitted by the model (i.e., same per-token billing), or do you apply a separate per-second/session metric for streaming?

2) Rounding / aggregation: the CSV is per-request. If a single user sends 3 short requests in 1 second, does Redwood round at the request level, or do you aggregate per-session and round once? We want predictable monthly bills when we commit.

3) Burst grace and overage: can you confirm how burst windows are treated? Is there a soft buffer before overage kicks in for committed customers?

Attached: DataWave_Usage_Export.csv (sample).

Would appreciate a short note on each point — happy to jump on a 30m call.

Best,
Amy Liu
Head of Platform Partnerships
DataWave Inc.
[Attachment: DataWave_Usage_Export.csv (csv)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Amy Liu <amy@datawave.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-25T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Metering questions for hosted commit tiers

Amy — thanks for the export and great questions. High level answers below and I copied Ben (sales ops) for the detailed math and Marissa (legal) for contract language.

- Streaming: we bill streamed output tokens at the same per-token rate as non-streamed requests; we do not add a separate per-second charge for streamed output. Input tokens (prompts) are billable under the same rules.

- Rounding/aggregation: by default we round per-request to the nearest token and sum across the billing period. For customers with a commit we can offer aggregation at the session level (one rounding operation per session) to reduce rounding noise — this is what most large streaming customers prefer.

- Burst grace: for committed tiers we include a 5% monthly buffer (credits) to absorb spikes before overage. We also provide a conditional burst policy where short-lived peaks within a 10-minute rolling window are allowed without immediate overage charging; sustained usage above commit triggers normal overage rates.

I'll attach our current pricing summary for reference. If DataWave is comfortable with these rules we can propose language.

Attached: RW_Pricing_Summary_v3.pdf (pdf)

Cheers,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Amy Liu <amy@datawave.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-26T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Metering questions for hosted commit tiers — examples and math

Amy, Rishi — quick worked examples to make the behavior concrete. I pulled a tiny sample from the CSV and applied two metering modes: request-level rounding and session-level aggregation.

Example A (request-level rounding):
- Req1: 12.4 tokens -> billed 12
- Req2: 0.7 tokens -> billed 1
- Req3: 3.9 tokens -> billed 4
Total billed = 17 tokens

Example B (session-level aggregation):
- Sum raw tokens across session = 16.999 -> billed 17 tokens (single rounding)

Net: for high-frequency short requests session-level aggregation reduces rounding up by ~0.5–1% in our samples.

Streaming nuance: streaming output is billed per emitted token. We do not meter by time. There is one exception — for long audio-only sessions where you do continuous transcription and token emission is very sparse, we can discuss a hybrid (minimum per-session floor) for committed customers.

Attached: redline_commit_terms.docx (proposed language + examples)

If useful I can create a spreadsheet mapping DataWave's historical volume into commit tiers and show estimated monthly bill with and without session aggregation. Want me to produce that?

Best,
Ben Carter
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — that helps. Two follow-ups: 

1) The hybrid floor for sparse audio sessions sounds promising. Can you propose a numeric floor (e.g., minimum 0.5 token/sec or a 10-token/session floor) so our finance team can model it?

2) For the session-level aggregation, does Redwood require a session id header to be passed, or do you infer sessions based on connection/stream id? We run multi-tenant routing and want to ensure we can provide clean session IDs if needed.

Also, our legal team will want explicit contract language for the 5% burst buffer and the 10-minute rolling window. Can you have Marissa draft that and share redlines?

Appreciate the clarity — a spreadsheet conversion of our last 3 months into commit tiers would be extremely helpful before we sign.

Best,
Amy

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Amy Liu <amy@datawave.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-27T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed contract text for billable tokens and rounding

Amy — draft language below that we think captures the operational behavior discussed. Please review and flag any issues.

--- Contract excerpt (draft) ---
"Billable units: Customer will be billed for billable tokens, defined as the sum of tokens generated by the model (output tokens) and tokens included in the customer's request payload (input tokens). Token counts will be measured per request and rounded to the nearest whole token unless Customer and Redwood agree to session-level aggregation, in which case token counts will be summed across a session and rounded once per session.

Streaming: Streamed output is billed on a per-token basis; no separate per-second or per-session time-based charge will apply. For long-running, low-emission audio sessions, the parties may agree to a minimum per-session floor (e.g., X tokens per session) which will be specified in the applicable Order Form.

Burst buffer and overage: Committed customers will receive a monthly buffer equal to 5% of the committed token volume. Short-term bursts under the agreed burst policy (10-minute rolling window) will not immediately trigger overage charges; sustained overages will be billed at the agreed overage rate.
---

If that looks good we can add it as an amendment to the master order and insert the numeric min-session floor once you give us a target.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

- Fallback policy: propose we add a fallback rule that if session IDs are missing or malformed, we default to request-level rounding for that usage and flag it for reconciliation. That avoids silent mismatches.
